# OTPilot

> Password manager with built-in 2FA. Fills your password and your 2FA code on any login page. End-to-end encrypted, synced across devices, free to start.

OTPilot is a Chrome extension that keeps your passwords and your 2FA (TOTP) codes together. On a login page it fills the username and password, then the 2FA code — no phone, no copying six digits. It also detects 2FA setup pages and saves the account in one click.

## Versions

- 2.1 (October 2026): OTPilot for AI agents — an MCP server (`@otpilot/mcp`) lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP agent sign in and run commands with the accounts the user allows, without the agent seeing a password or a code
- 2.0: a full password manager — passwords filled on login pages, an end-to-end encrypted vault (passwords, 2FA, notes, servers, API keys, custom fields), sync, team sharing and imports
- 1.x: 2FA code auto-fill only (accounts move into the 2.0 vault automatically)

## Key features

- Fills passwords and 2FA codes on login pages; offers to save new sign-ins and updated passwords
- Detects 2FA setup pages automatically — reads otpauth:// URIs and QR codes from the page
- Secure notes, servers and API credentials, with custom fields and related items
- End-to-end encrypted: the vault is encrypted on your device under a master password
- Sync across devices (Personal plan); import from Chrome, 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass and more
- Team sharing: share a whole item or chosen fields end-to-end encrypted, or share live 2FA codes without the secret
- AI agents (new in 2.1): Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP agent can sign in and run commands with the accounts you allow, without the secrets ever reaching the model
- Open source, no telemetry

## Compared to alternatives

- Google Authenticator / Authy: require your phone every login. OTPilot fills automatically.
- 1Password / Bitwarden built-in TOTP: require cloud accounts. OTPilot is local by default.
- Manual copy-paste: OTPilot eliminates this entirely.

## Team sharing

OTPilot supports sharing TOTP codes with teammates without exposing the underlying secret. The owner uploads the secret encrypted with an independent sharing key. The backend generates the TOTP code on demand for recipients, who never receive the secret itself. Revocation is instant: the owner removes a recipient and their access is cut immediately. Sharing whole items (passwords, notes, fields) is separate and end-to-end encrypted: the server never sees them.

Invitation flow:
- With an account: invite appears directly in the extension
- Without an account: recipient receives an email with a link to install the extension; the pending invite is automatically linked to their email on signup

## AI agents (2.1)

The user manages everything in the extension; the agent only talks to the OTPilot MCP server on the user's computer. Its tools never return a secret: it signs in to websites (password + 2FA, on the account's own site only) and hands the session to the agent's browser, or runs a command with secrets injected as environment variables and scrubbed from the output.

- Two approvals: an agent connects with a verification code checked in the extension and gets no accounts; each account is then allowed per agent, with a scope (2FA code only, whole sign-in, chosen fields) and a duration, or "ask every time"
- Team plans: accounts teammates share with the user (directly or through a collection) can be allowed too; the agent's copy follows the shared item and goes when the user loses access to it
- Each allowed account is encrypted for that agent's own key (kept in the OS keychain); the server only stores ciphertext; revoking an agent cuts its access
- Activity log of every use; requests show on the extension's badge
- Connect an agent: `npx -y @otpilot/mcp@latest connect` (prints a verification code; approve it in the extension's Agents view)
- Limit: an agent that runs commands decides what they do and could try to reveal a secret on purpose; scrubbing, 2FA-only scopes and per-use approval narrow it

## Plans

- Free: unlimited 2FA codes, up to 50 passwords, notes and other items, on one device; AI agents: 1 agent, up to 3 accounts
- Personal ($3/month or $30/year): unlimited items, end-to-end encrypted sync across devices, unlimited AI agents
- Team ($8/workspace/month or $80/year, 5 seats included, +$2 per extra seat/month): sharing with teammates and collections
